decision.thesis: All cash, sixteenth session, the second ramp decision, recorded before Bursa's Thursday open on Wednesday's settled closes; the 2026-09-22 feedback page offers no cause for any name; claim: nothing in the fundable universe beats cash over 21 sessions.

mistakes: **The learning store still dates yesterday's prediction before the decision.** `data/learning.db` records `made_at` **2026-09-22T22:30:00Z** for `paper-2026-09-22-allcash-21d-33c5` (decision date 2026-09-22), while `data/paper.db` records its `decided_at` as **2026-09-23T02:33:01Z**. PR #76's real-clock stamp applies to new rows and did not restamp this one. Tonight's row shows the fix working: `paper-2026-09-23-allcash-21d-b999` has `made_at` and `decided_at` both at **2026-09-23T22:53:55Z**.

**Last night's page reported a mark count the ledger no longer holds.** It said *19 marks* for the book opened 2026-09-08 (decision 2026-09-22, `paper-2026-09-22-allcash-21d-33c5`). After the migration the status prints 14, and the six dropped days were weekends. The earlier pages' session counts (*fifteenth session* on 09-22) were counted by calendar, not from marks, so they stand.
lessons: A migration that rewrites a ledger's history rewrites the pages that quoted it. A count copied onto a page (19 marks) is true only of the ledger version it was read from, so the page needs the commit it was read at.

A decision's clock is auditable only when every store stamps the same instant. Tonight's row has one timestamp in both stores and yesterday's has two, four hours apart. Restamping the one old row would make the record look consistent but would not change when the decision was actually taken.

A control book first invested on a cost-bearing day starts behind. The −0.83% on its first mark includes entry fees, FX spread and slippage that the decided book, all in cash, has not paid, and a grade that ignores this favours cash.
